The A0 note says 'neither library has ... a Picard functor or Picard scheme (the nearest object is Tau Ceti's `LineBundleClass X` ... still without inverses)'. The summary says there is no 'Picard functor ... anywhere'. All three are false as written. Mathlib has the Picard group of a commutative ring, which is Pic(Spec R), as a group with inverses. It is functorial along ring maps and packaged as a functor CommSemiRingCat ⥤ CommGrpCat, i.e. the absolute Picard functor on affine schemes. Mathlib also has the relative Picard group Pic(A/R) = ker(Pic R → Pic A) and the class-group comparison. This is the Pic(T) of affine test schemes that the relative Picard functor T ↦ Pic(X_T)/Pic(T) is built from, and it is nearer to a 'Picard functor' than LineBundleClass. On the elliptic side, Mathlib's point-to-class-group map is the field-level shadow of E ≅ Pic⁰. The targets stay absent; what is wrong is the stated reason.
